articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos España vs República Checa
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y República Checa en el Carlos Tartiere, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League 2026-27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y República Checa en el Carlos Tartiere, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League 2026-27
articles.body: España recibe a la República Checa este sábado en Oviedo, en la tercera jornada del Grupo A3. La campeona del mundo llega lanzada. Ganó 3-2 a Inglaterra en Wembley y goleó 4-1 a Croacia en Sevilla, con doblete de Lamine Yamal, por lo que lidera el grupo con puntuación perfecta. La selección de Santi Denia, en cambio, suma dos derrotas. Cayó 2-1 ante Croacia y 2-0 ante Inglaterra en Praga, un partido en el que jugó más de una hora con diez por la expulsión de Pavel Šulc. Favorito para el partido entre España vs República Checa Las casas de apuestas no tienen dudas. Codere paga la victoria de España a cuota 1.06, por 9.5 del empate y 35.00 del triunfo checo. Los precedentes refuerzan la lectura: España no ha perdido nunca contra la República Checa desde la separación de Checoslovaquia (cinco victorias y dos empates) y ha ganado los cuatro partidos que ha jugado como local ante este rival. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan ofrece algo más de valor que el del ganador. España es una máquina ofensiva, pero no ha dejado su portería a cero en esta Nations League. Encajó dos goles en Wembley y uno de Beljo ante Croacia. La República Checa, por su parte, marcó en su estreno ante Croacia y mantiene su amenaza a balón parado, un recurso que puede castigar a una defensa española que está probando piezas. Sin embargo, los checos llegan sin Schick ni Souček y se quedaron en blanco ante Inglaterra, así que la balanza no está clara. En las apuestas deportivas, Codere paga el sí a 2.75 y el no a 1.4. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta a un partido con ventaja española, pero con un tope razonable. España ha anotado cuatro y tres goles en sus dos partidos, aunque los dos han tenido cinco goles en total por los tantos encajados. La República Checa, por el contrario, se mueve en marcadores cortos: dos goles en sus dos encuentros contando los dos partidos (uno marcado y cuatro encajados, con diez hombres en el último). Con un rival que sabe defenderse y tiene que competir por un resultado digno, lo lógico es un partido de pocos goles para el rival. Codere paga el más de 3.5 goles a 1.8 y el menos de 3.5 a 1.95. Equipo con más córners El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante, y aquí la clave es quién tendrá el balón. España domina las posesiones largas y, ante Croacia, ya había botado seis saques de esquina en el tramo final del partido, uno de los cuales acabó en el gol de Pubill. La República Checa, sin Souček, se ha mostrado muy replegada: ante Inglaterra tuvo un 33.8 % de posesión y apenas seis disparos, con 22 de su rival. Si Denia plantea de nuevo una línea baja, España acumulará llegadas y córners. El pronóstico es que España será el equipo con más córners a 1.13, por 7.5 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Neeraj Chauhan clinches recurve bronze, defeats Dhiraj Bommadevara in all-India clash at Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan won the bronze medal in the men's recurve individual event at the Asian Games 2026 after defeating compatriot
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan won the bronze medal in the men's recurve individual event at the Asian Games 2026 after defeating compatriot Dhiraj Bommadevara 6-4 at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square on Saturday.In an all-Indian medal contest, Chauhan held his nerve to finish ahead of Bommadevara and claim the bronze medal.Chauhan started strongly and won the first game 29-26.Bommadevara hit 7, 9 and 10 for a total of 26, while Chauhan shot 10, 9 and 10 to score 29.Bommadevara hit back in the second set. He scored 28, including a 10 and an X, while Chauhan managed 27. Bommadevara won the set 2-0 to level the match at 2-2.The third set went Chauhan's way. He scored 28 with an X, 9 and 9, while Bommadevara scored 29 with an X, 9 and 10.Bommadevara won the set 2-0, moving ahead 4-2.Chauhan then responded in the fourth set. He produced 30, hitting 10, X and 10, while Bommadevara scored 28. Chauhan took the set 2-0, bringing the match level at 4-4.The fifth and final set decided the bronze medal.Chauhan delivered when it mattered most, shooting 29 with an X, 9 and another X. Bommadevara scored 28 with 8, 10 and 10.Chauhan won the final set 2-0 and finished the match with a 6-4 victory.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 India medal winners: Full list of athletes and medals till October 3
articles.summary: India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze
articles.body: India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s Gold Medal Winners at Asian Games 2026No.Athlete/TeamSportEventMedal1India women’s cricket teamCricketWomen’s T20🥇 Gold2Kamaljeet & Suruchi SinghShooting10m air pistol mixed team🥇 Gold3India women’s kabaddi teamKabaddiWomen’s tournament🥇 Gold4India men’s kabaddi teamKabaddiMen’s tournament🥇 Gold5Neeru DhandaShootingWomen’s trap🥇 Gold6Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary, Vithya RamrajAthleticsWomen’s 4x400m relay🥇 Gold7Chikitha Taniparthi, Prithika Pradeep, Jyothi Surekha VennamArcheryWomen’s compound team🥇 Gold8Chikitha Taniparthi & Sahil JadhavArcheryMixed compound team🥇 Gold9Kynan Chenai & Neeru DhandaShootingMixed trap team🥇 Gold10Sahil Jadhav, Kushal Dalal, Ganesh Mani Ratnam ThirumuruArcheryMen’s compound team🥇 Gold11Lovlina BorgohainBoxingWomen’s 75kg🥇 Gold12Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma, Kumkum MohodArcheryWomen’s recurve team🥇 Gold13Parveen HoodaBoxingWomen’s 65kg🥇 Gold14Ankush PanghalBoxingMen’s 80kg🥇 Gold15Sujeet KalkalWrestlingMen’s freestyle 65kg🥇 Gold16India women’s hockey teamHockeyWomen’s tournament🥇 Gold17Kumkum MohodArcheryWomen’s individual recurve🥇 Gold18Pranavi UrsGolfWomen’s individual🥇 GoldIndia’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. articles.title: Deepak Punia holds off Ganbaatar 2-1 to clinch Asian Games wrestling bronze
articles.summary: Deepak Punia won the bronze medal in the men's 97kg freestyle wrestling event at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, beating Mongolia's
articles.body: Deepak Punia won the bronze medal in the men's 97kg freestyle wrestling event at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, beating Mongolia's Gankhuyag Ganbaatar 2-1 in the bronze medal bout.Punia took a 2-0 lead after scoring two points in the opening period. Ganbaatar managed to get one point in the second half, but Punia defended well to protect his lead and complete the win.The bronze is Punia's second Asian Games medal. He had won silver in the 86kg freestyle event at the Hangzhou 2022 Games.Punia's medal came on the same day Aman Sehrawat won gold in the men's 57kg freestyle event. Aman beat DPR Korea's World Champion Han Chong Song 11-7 in the final to claim his second Asian Games medal, having won bronze in the same category at Hangzhou 2022.The final was closely fought, with both wrestlers staying level before Aman scored the first points to take the lead.Aman defended well against Han's repeated attacks and quickly moved 6-1 ahead just after half-time with a series of well-timed attacking moves. However, Han responded with a strong counterattack and scored six points in quick succession to take a 7-6 lead.Aman then turned the bout around with an important move that earned him four points. He was awarded another point after Han's unsuccessful challenge, putting Aman back in front.Punia's bronze is India's third medal in freestyle wrestling at the Asian Games 2026, after Sujeet Kalkal won gold in the 65kg category on Friday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. As the college football season hits Week 5, the separation process has begun in earnest and a handful of key matchups this week will continue that work.

At the top of that list is a key Big Ten showdown with No. 5 Ohio State traveling to face No. 14 Iowa, which is coming off a big win at Michigan. The Buckeyes already have a loss on their resume thanks to Texas and will try to avoid dropping to 3-2 in a tough environment.

The SEC slate features a pair of ranked unbeatens facing off as No. 16 Mississippi State hosts No. 7 Alabama, while No. 8 Florida also will look to stay perfect as it travels to No. 25 Missouri.

Other unbeaten teams facing potentially tricky road trips include No. 3 Notre Dame at North Carolina, No. 10 BYU at TCU, No. 4 Miami at Clemson and No. 12 Texas Tech at Colorado.

articles.title: Friendly defeat in the international break
articles.summary: 2-1 loss to FC Blau-Weiß LinzAs part of the opening of a new sports facility in Pischelsdorf, our Red Bulls played a friendly match there against FC Blau-Wei...
articles.body:
As part of the opening of a new sports facility in Pischelsdorf, our Red Bulls played a friendly match there against FC Blau-Weiß Linz. The clash with the 2. Liga leaders ended in a narrow 1–2 defeat.

Early on, Edmund Baidoo headed our boys into the lead following a fine assist by Konate. The Ghanaian also hit the crossbar shortly afterwards, while Dominik Schmid and Stefan Lainer failed to convert good chances. Linz captain Manuel Maranda equalized with a header just before the break. Shortly after the restart, the Linz side turned the match around, scoring in the 47th minute to seal a 2–1 win.

We wrapped up a good week of training with a genuinely good friendly match, even if the final result wasn't what we wanted. That's a bit frustrating. However, we were able to implement much of what we had planned and handled many situations well, especially in possession. We also created enough chances to win the game. Now we have two days off before we can fully prepare for the next block of important matches.

The following 10 international players were unavailable today: Abubakr Barry, Kevin Boma, Aboubacar Camara, Filip Matijasevic, Bartosz Mazurek, John Mellberg, Leandro Morgalla, Nikola Sarcevic, Haris Tabakovic and Valentin Zabransky.

Missing due to injury were Enrique Aguilar (thigh), Soumaila Diabate (thigh), Johannes Moser (adductor), Justin Omoregie (ankle), Damir Redzic (ankle), Nikolas Veratschnig (knee) and Christian Zawieschitzky (adductor).

On the positive side, Gaoussou Diakite returned to action after a long injury lay-off.

FC Liefering youngsters Filip Aleksic, Teo Hupfauf, Julian Hussauf, Ilia Ivanschitz, Riquelme, Lassina Traore and Jakob Zangerl were also included in the squad for the friendly match.

The team has the weekend off from training before preparations begin on Monday for the upcoming ADMIRAL Bundesliga match against GAK.

articles.title: Bayern Munich formulating goalkeeper plan for 2026/27
articles.summary: FC Bayern has a strategy for the goalkeeper position.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich is beginning to plan for a major change in its goalkeeping department, with Manuel Neuer and Sven Ulreich both potentially heading toward retirement at the end of the season.

According to Kicker's Frank Linkesch (via @iMiaSanMia ), Bayern Munich plans to hold talks with both goalkeepers about their futures during either the November international break or the winter break. The current expectation is that both Neuer and Ulreich will retire when the season concludes.

If that happens, Jonas Urbig is expected to take over as Bayern Munich's clear No. 1 next season. The club is already looking at options for a goalkeeper to serve as Urbig's backup.

Bayern Munich has established a specific profile for the position: the new No. 2 should be experienced, comfortable accepting a backup role, relatively inexpensive to sign, and capable of contributing with his feet. That last requirement is particularly important under Vincent Kompany, who expects his goalkeepers to be comfortable in possession, even during training.

No goalkeeper has been approached at this stage, but FC Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, Fulham's Bernd Leno, and Hoffenheim's Oliver Baumann are among the names being discussed internally. While Leno and Baumann are older veterans, Dahmen is still just 28 years old and may be more inclined to remain a No. 1 goalkeeper with FC Augsburg.

Bayern Munich is also taking its time with the No. 3 position, which could ultimately be filled by an academy goalkeeper or an external signee.
